response.justification: The candidate is an experienced, versatile senior engineer, but the profile is a poor match for this role's mandatory requirements. Hands-on C++ work is limited to roughly six months at National Instruments (2014–2015), over a decade ago, versus the required 5–10 years of current C++ on Windows. The stack is overwhelmingly web/backend (TypeScript, Node.js, DLang, Ember), development appears Linux/macOS-oriented rather than Windows, and SQL exposure is listed generically (MySQL/MongoDB) with no SQL Server or Oracle depth. There is no fixed income, derivatives, investment banking, or capital markets domain experience; RIDE Capital is fintech/investment-adjacent but not capital-markets systems. Strong engineering fundamentals, testing culture, and communication skills are evident, but they do not offset the core technical and domain gaps.
strengths: Strong engineering fundamentals: TDD, CI/CD, DevOps, low-latency systems work
Excellent communication evidenced by workshops, conference talks, and courses
Broad polyglot experience including some C/C++ and performance-critical services
concerns: Only ~6 months of C++ experience, and it was over 10 years ago
No fixed income, derivatives, or capital markets/investment banking domain exposure
No demonstrated Windows platform focus or SQL Server/Oracle depth

key_factors.factor: Overall senior engineering craft and communication
